description: Help us build the ultimate GPS for Mars! We are competing in the Martian Map challenge to engineer a visual navigation tool that keeps astronauts alive during surface excursions. Looking for coders who love data wrangling, designers who want to map a planet, and anyone ready to drink too much caffeine and hack all weekend. Hit us up if you want to join!
summary:
MARSCOPE is an interactive Mars exploration and decision-support platform designed to help future human explorers evaluate terrain and plan safer surface traversals. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, it combines interactive 2D mapping, 3D terrain visualization, terrain analysis, and intelligent route optimization in a unified interface.

Using the A* pathfinding algorithm, MARSCOPE generates and compares two route alternatives: a risk-aware route that considers terrain-related risks and a distance-focused route that prioritizes shorter traversal. Explainable route metrics, including distance and average terrain roughness, help users understand the trade-offs between safety and efficiency.

The platform aims to make complex planetary terrain information easier to interpret and turn it into actionable exploration insights. Its modular architecture also provides a foundation for future predictive hazard intelligence as suitable validated datasets become available.
details:
MARSCOPE: Project Details

1. Overview

MARSCOPE is an interactive planetary exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support future human exploration of Mars. It provides an integrated environment where users can visualize Martian terrain, examine surface characteristics, and compare potential traversal routes.

The initial focus is Jezero Crater, a scientifically important region explored by NASA's Perseverance rover.

2. Interactive 2D and 3D Terrain Visualization

MARSCOPE combines an interactive 2D Mars map with a 3D terrain visualization environment. Users can explore the selected region, understand elevation variations, and observe the relationship between terrain features and potential traversal paths.

The 3D environment is built using Three.js and React Three Fiber, while the 2D mapping interface uses React Leaflet.

3. Intelligent Route Planning Using A*

The platform implements the A* pathfinding algorithm to identify alternative routes between a selected starting point and destination.

Two route alternatives are generated:

  • Risk-aware route: incorporates terrain-related risk factors into route evaluation to prioritize comparatively safer traversal.
  • Distance-focused route: prioritizes a shorter traversal path.

This comparison helps users understand that the shortest route is not necessarily the most suitable route for exploration.

4. Explainable Route Intelligence

MARSCOPE provides a route comparison interface that presents useful metrics, including:

  • Total route distance
  • Average terrain roughness
  • Comparative route characteristics

These metrics make the route-planning process more interpretable and help users evaluate the trade-offs between traversal efficiency and terrain-related risk.

5. Terrain and Hazard Intelligence

Terrain analysis contributes to the assessment of surface conditions and route suitability. The platform also includes environmental and hazard information panels.

Future development will expand this component into predictive hazard intelligence using validated historical and spatial datasets. Potential extensions include identifying hazardous terrain conditions and estimating changing environmental risks. These predictive capabilities are a planned extension rather than a fully validated forecasting system in the current prototype.

6. Technology and Architecture

Frontend

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite

3D Visualization

  • Three.js
  • React Three Fiber
  • Drei

2D Mapping

  • React Leaflet
  • Leaflet

Backend

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • NumPy
  • Rasterio
  • SciPy

Algorithms and Analysis

  • A* pathfinding
  • Terrain analysis
  • Risk-based route evaluation
  • Route comparison metrics

Development Tools

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • npm
  • Python

7. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation of MARSCOPE is the integration of interactive planetary visualization, terrain-aware pathfinding, and explainable route comparison in a single exploration platform.

Rather than presenting only a map or a shortest-path result, MARSCOPE allows users to compare alternative traversal strategies and understand the factors influencing route selection.

Its modular architecture is designed to support future integration of additional planetary datasets and predictive intelligence.

8. Intended Impact

MARSCOPE aims to make planetary terrain information more accessible and useful for exploration planning. It provides a prototype foundation for evaluating surface conditions, comparing traversal alternatives, and supporting more informed decisions during future human Mars missions.

The system is a research and planning prototype, not a certified operational navigation or astronaut safety system.
